correctness.rationale: For total weight at most six, a layer of weight at most two cannot defend its many zero vertices without forcing excessive matched weight in the opposite layer, so both clique layers have weight at least three. At equality each layer has weight exactly three. The profiles 2+1 and 1+1+1 are excluded by the defining zero- and one-vertex conditions, leaving one label 3 per layer. The quasi-total isolated-positive rule forces the two labels 3 to be adjacent, hence matched. The matched pair construction is feasible. A definition-level exhaustive checker verifies every labeling for n=3,4,5 and exactly matches the classification for n=4,5.

value.rationale: Complete prisms K_n square K_2 form a standard unbounded Cartesian-product family. The theorem is not a routine instance calculation: it proves a constant parameter value six for all n at least four and completely determines the equality structure, with exactly one optimum per matching edge. The layer-weight obstruction and matching-edge rigidity expose how the quasi-total isolated-positive rule changes double Roman optimization on a natural dense product family.
